newsitem.title: USA: Muni credit spreads tighten in past week - Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni credit spreads tighten in past week - Delphis.

text.p: Credit spreads for long-term and intermediate municipal bonds tightened slightly over the week ended Thursday, Delphis Hanover Corp said on Friday.
The spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated 30-year bonds tightened five basis points to 60 basis points, while the 10-year spread tightened to 70 from 75.
One-year spreads, however, held steady at 65 basis points.
The tightening came as yields on lower-rated investment-grade munis fell slightly and top-rated bonds remained unchanged.
One-year Aaa-rated bond yields were flat at 3.70 percent, while Baa-rated one-years held at 4.35 percent.
Average yields were unchanged at 4.50 percent for Aaa-rated 10-year munis, and dropped five basis points, to 5.20 percent, for Baa 10-years, Delphis said.
Long-term municipals lagged the Treasury market over the week.
The yield on the government long bond fell 14 basis points during the period to 6.30 percent, after dropping five basis points the week before.

At the same time, thirty-year Aaa-rated municipal yields were unchanged for the second consecutive week at 5.25 percent. Yields fell five basis points for 30-year, Baa-rated bonds, dropping to 5.85 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis yielded 83.3 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday, compared to 81.5 percent the week before.
The yield curve between one-year and 30-year bonds in the triple-A category held steady at 155 basis points, while the Baa yield curve flattened five to 150 basis points.
